subject: Media Literacy
title: The Profit Motive and News Quality
description: A fast breakdown of The Profit Motive and News Quality for builders.

hook.text: An investigation costs $500,000 and takes a year. A clickbait listicle costs $50 and takes an hour. Guess which wins.

buildup.text: The profit motive pushes news organizations toward cheaper, faster, more sensational content.

discovery.text: Investigative journalism — the most important kind — is the most expensive and least commercially viable.

twist.text: Profit-driven newsrooms don't bias toward left or right. They bias toward whatever generates the most engagement.

climax.text: The deepest bias in media isn't political. It's commercial — favoring stories that attract attention over those that matter.

punchline.text: The biggest bias isn't left or right. It's profitable.

quiz.question: What is the deepest structural bias in commercial media?
options: The commercial bias toward stories that generate engagement over importance
